title: SSP-0 — Projects Subject Assignment Foundation Delivery
summary: keep document subject information read-only and move Projects folder assignment into a focused modal foundation extended by SSP-1
content_html:
SSP-0 — Projects Subject Assignment Foundation Delivery

Status And Purpose

SSP-0 is complete as the standalone foundation for SSP-1, consuming the completed SSC-1 — Unified Sub-Scope Customisation Contract Delivery. The accepted SSP-0.0 sanity note fixed the Projects None/Folder boundary; SSP-0.1 evidence records the exact read-only projection, SSP-0.2 evidence records focused assignment, and SSP-0.3 evidence records final verification and ownership transfer. SSP-1 owns Work/Series subject meaning and state projection; SSP-4 owns explicit creation and acceptance of the later analysis/works collection.

The generic metadata modal now retains universal document fields and independently configured owners while Projects folder_path is assigned through the focused modal. The passive Info view receives the exact active sub-scope document and Projects None/Folder subject state. SSC-1 shipped the single accepted sub-scope customisation contract. SSP-0 declares the authoring_subject DocsSubScopeAssignableFieldGroup before SSP-1 extends its server-owned fields with work_id and series_id; Info remains read-only and subject fields remain outside the generic metadata modal.

Complete Outcome

On the local Manage route, metadata-info displays one compact read-only authoring-subject summary for the exact active {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} target. SSP-0 supplies None or Folder evidence from the current Projects projection. SSP-1 extends the same passive view contract with Work, Series, malformed, and conflicting subject states after it owns those meanings. Info contains no form fields, picker results, save lifecycle, revision receipt, or write service. Public routes retain their current compact metadata policy and receive no private subject projection or management capability.

Only a sub-scope whose resolved definition declares DocsSubScopeAssignableFieldGroup(group_id="authoring_subject", ...) offers the quick Assign subject action. dotlineform/projects is currently the only registered sub-scope intended to gain that declaration. The server resolves it with sub_scope_customisation_assignable_field_groups() and the browser checks its projected ID with hasDocsViewerAssignableFieldGroup(); the concrete field names remain server-owned. The action opens a focused modal whose owners include option selection, value acquisition, confirmation, exact target, source revision, mutation feedback, and cancellation.

SSP-0 moves the existing Projects folder_path editor into that modal and initially supports None or Folder using the current source contract. SSP-1 later extends the same modal to the complete None, Folder, Work, or Series authoring group when it adds work_id and series_id meaning, normalized state, associations, and Manage cues.

SSP-4 explicitly creates and configures the later analysis/works collection when collection-aware Copy is delivered. That stage proves retained Work/Series metadata displays through the SSP-1 read projection while the collection advertises no assignable authoring-subject capability. SSP-0 neither creates that collection nor treats it as current acceptance evidence.

Analysis Tags group and future tag_id editing remain owned by the independent Tag feature. TDL-0 — Tag Document Metadata Authoring Refactor Delivery removes the remaining Tag group exception from Edit metadata through its own configured modal. SSP-0 does not move Tags controls, create a cross-collection metadata editor, or make TDL depend on this delivery.

Assignment Modal Reuse

The two subject value families reuse accepted interaction and normalization components rather than creating new discovery behavior:

  • Folder accepts a Finder-copied absolute path or local file: URL, reusing the local-folder paste normalizer to confine it beneath the configured Projects base and store only the decoded portable relative folder_path. The pure resolver may be extracted from its current Source Editor owner so the modal does not import an insertion workflow.
  • Work and Series, added in SSP-1, reuse the existing Catalogue target support, matching, and accessible picker-list components behind Add catalogue token. The subject modal writes only the selected canonical ID; it does not ask for token title text or insert Markdown.
  • None explicitly clears the current subject fields through the same confirmed mutation.

The Info panel previously hosted Semantic Token search controls before catalogue discovery moved to the focused Add catalogue token modal. Subject assignment follows that accepted direction: Info reports the current value; the modal performs search, resolution, selection, and confirmation.

Projects Subject Rules

The complete Projects modal presents one option group because all choices answer the same authoring question: what is this document about?

None
Folder  -> paste and resolve a Finder URL/path
Work    -> search and select one canonical Work
Series  -> search and select one canonical Series

An explicit save writes the selected canonical field and removes the other subject fields. Existing malformed or conflicting source remains visible in read-only Info until the author explicitly opens the modal and resolves it; opening Info or opening/cancelling the modal never assigns precedence or repairs source.

The quick action is currently available only in dotlineform/projects because that resolved sub-scope contribution declares the assignable subject group. It is not activated by a literal collection-name comparison, inferred from the mere presence of a subject field, copied into analysis/works, exposed by public routes, or generalized to every collection. Read/display support and quick-assignment support remain separate capabilities.

Delivery Discipline

This is a bounded Projects UI and mutation-foundation delivery. It consumes SSC-1's DocsSubScopeAssignableFieldGroup, exact-target, metadata, browser-composition, and access-safe capability projection, then reuses the Projects customisation normalizer, local-folder resolver, management modal shell, revision receipts, atomic source mutation, and targeted rebuild seams. The browser action, modal, and service resolve availability and accepted fields from the exact sub-scope definition and projected authoring_subject group. It does not introduce a generic schema editor, editable Info contribution, unrestricted cross-collection assignment service, relationship framework, internal Info navigation, or public runtime capability.

SSP-0.0 is a short scope-and-spec sanity gate. Each implementation stage ends with focused evidence and an independent code/diff review before the next stage begins.

Delivery Steps

SSP-0.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [x] Confirm the shipped sub_scope_customisation, DocsSubScopeAssignableFieldGroup, authoring_subject, exact-target, metadata, and access-safe browser capability contracts; then sanity-check focused subject assignment, local-folder URL/path resolution, revision-safe mutation, generic metadata separation, and public isolation against current broad owners.
  • [x] Confirm the likely blast radius across hosted-view context, active sub-scope target projection, Projects report/detail contribution, management modal shell, folder normalizer, Projects mutation, targeted rebuild, and current metadata/customisation tests.
  • [x] Confirm the deliverables: read-only subject summary, Projects-only Assign subject action and modal, None/Folder assignment, generic-modal Projects cleanup, SSP-1 Work/Series extension seam, focused evidence, and durable Info/management documentation transfer.
  • [x] Stop for review if the outcome requires inline Info editing, a generic field-schema engine, broad application-state access, literal scope/sub-scope name checks, an unrestricted cross-collection write service, duplicated folder normalization, public subject controls, or Tag workflow changes.
  • [x] Resolve the review finding by retaining Work/Series meaning in SSP-1 and making analysis/works creation and acceptance an explicit SSP-4 action.

Checkpoint: a concise sanity note confirms implementation fit, broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, exact-target behavior, public isolation, and the SSP-1 handoff. Stop before implementation approval.

SSP-0.1 — Add Exact Read-Only Subject Information

  • [x] Project the exact active managed-document target into metadata-info, including a sub-scope detail document rather than its parent report or currently selected index row.
  • [x] Render a compact read-only subject summary from explicit projected state without reparsing Markdown or hydrating write-capable services in the Info view.
  • [x] Project Assign subject action availability from the exact sub-scope's declared assignable subject group; prove the current Projects registration enables it while other configured collections and public routes retain their declared capabilities.
  • [x] Preserve current outside-context view selection and the Info shell's view-agnostic hosting model.

Checkpoint: focused exact-target, wrong-target, None/Folder state, view lifecycle, Projects action eligibility, other-collection, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms Info remains a passive exact-document projection. Stop before SSP-0.2.

SSP-0.2 — Move Projects Folder Assignment Into The Modal

  • [x] Add the focused Projects Assign subject modal with initial None/Folder options, exact target and source revision, confirmation, cancellation, and contained status/error behavior.
  • [x] Reuse or cleanly extract the existing local-folder resolver so a pasted absolute path or file: URL becomes the canonical portable folder_path; retain confinement and invalid-input behavior.
  • [x] Add a capability-restricted subject mutation that resolves the exact sub-scope configuration, accepts only its declared assignable subject keys, preserves revision conflict and atomic replacement, and triggers the exact required rebuild without a collection-name branch.
  • [x] Remove Projects folder_path rendering and payload handling from Edit metadata after focused equivalence evidence confirms the modal owner.
  • [x] Preserve a clear extension seam for SSP-1 to add Work/Series options using the existing Catalogue target search and picker components without changing Info into an editor.

Checkpoint: focused modal, capability registration, folder resolution, invalid/outside path, clear, cancel, stale revision, exact-target, atomic-write, targeted-build, generic-metadata independence, Analysis action absence, and public-boundary evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms current quick-assignment availability comes from the Projects capability declaration rather than collection-name logic. Stop before SSP-0.3.

SSP-0.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [x] Run focused service, browser-module, route-boundary, source-lint, generated-doc, search, and whitespace checks proportional to the changed contracts.
  • [x] Verify rendered-document and Markdown-source contexts, Projects folder/no-subject states, unavailable management service, stale revision, cancel/clear behavior, and public read-only presentation.
  • [x] Perform the independent final code/delivery review and reconcile completion claims with exact evidence and omissions.
  • [x] Update Info Panel, Management Operations, and the current Projects customisation owner with the shipped read-only projection, modal assignment, mutation, reuse, and public-isolation rules.
  • [x] Update SSP-1 to consume the accepted modal and read-only Info contracts before adding Work/Series assignment and associations.

Completion Evidence

  • Info displays exact current subject evidence without inline controls or write services.
  • Only the currently registered dotlineform/projects assignable-subject capability exposes the quick Assign subject action and modal; the implementation contains no literal collection-name availability branch.
  • Projects None/Folder assignment retains accepted portable path normalization through its focused mutation.
  • Edit metadata no longer reads, renders, or submits Projects folder_path.
  • SSP-1 owns Work/Series read projection, and SSP-4 owns analysis/works creation plus read-only copied-subject acceptance.
  • Public routes retain their compact passive Info policy without subject metadata or management capability.
  • SSP-1 can extend the Projects modal with Catalogue Work/Series search while leaving Info read-only.
  • Tag group and Tag identity workflows remain outside SSP-0.
